conclusion: The first native load predicate passed to the one-per-canvas context-loss watcher retains the per-build lexical environment. Old NativeLevel/data/physics and large arrays remain after world disposal; nativeWorld itself is collected. This is bounded to the first native build per canvas, rather than a stage-ID cache, but retains a materially large mobile CPU graph.
snapshotOrder: No strong CDP target handle existed during collection/snapshot. Resolve snapshot IDs from WeakRefs only afterward, then releaseObjectGroup. No inventory render hook, geometry listeners, or per-frame weak polling were installed.
caveats: WeakRefs only show target reachability, not retained-byte totals.
The minimum known retained original native typed-array payload is11,077,610 bytes; JS face/block/nav/paint graphs and texture CPU buffers are additional and not quantified here.
BFS excludes weak and ephemeron-table edges. The reported canvas listener path requires neither and is directly backed by callback locations in the exact emitted native engine.
This is one candidate e4 LOW diagnostic, not a baseline/candidate timing comparison or hardware memory-residency test.
